label_scheme.scene: a concrete moment, observation, case, place or hypothetical the reader can picture
label_scheme.orientation: nut graf: what the piece is about, the question, why it matters, the short answer
label_scheme.method: how a study or investigation was actually done (who/what was studied, procedure, measurement, duration)
label_scheme.finding: what a study or analysis found (results, effect sizes)
label_scheme.explanation: how something works: mechanism, background science, definitions
label_scheme.context: history, prevalence/scale, stakes, who is affected, the field's state
label_scheme.complication: competing explanation, contrary result, a limitation or uncertainty that matters
label_scheme.voice: paragraph carried mainly by a quoted person's words (interview or written)
label_scheme.practical: what people actually do, or implications for practice/policy
label_scheme.payoff: closing paragraph(s) that return to the opening or deliver the final understanding

articles.title: The Brain Has a ‘Low-Power Mode’ That Blunts Our Senses
articles.note: device analogy, headline result and its perceptual cost up front; backfills prior hunger studies, then method-finding pairs across two crossheads; ends on what it means for lab practice and humans

articles.title: Last Hope Experiment Finds Evidence for Unknown Particles
articles.note: news-led feature: result and rival calculation in the first dozen paragraphs, then a long history-and-mechanism middle (g-factor, Brookhaven, two ways to compute hadron effects), a short reveal scene, and an ending that weighs competing readings

articles.title: Overexposure Distorted the Science of Mirror Neurons
articles.note: discovery scene in a 1991 lab, then a rise-and-fall history of the idea (hype, critique, debate, decline in papers), ending with recent mouse work that revives a narrower version; history-of-an-idea arc with almost no method detail

articles.title: The Webb Telescope Further Deepens the Biggest Controversy in Cosmology
articles.note: news peg and two rival teams up front, a history section on measuring distance, then a close account of one team's blinded three-method analysis (unblinding, errors found, three numbers), ending on newer independent methods; dense in method and finding

articles.title: The Unpredictable Abilities Emerging From Large AI Models
articles.note: opens on one benchmark puzzle (emoji movie), nut graf on emergent abilities, then a background block on models and scaling, the benchmark study and its breakthroughs, two rival explanations, and a risks section built on bias studies

articles.title: Free will: does refusing to believe in it make you a ‘bad’ person? Research is challenging this old idea
articles.note: researcher-written argument: reader-addressed hook, classic experiments told method-first, a long section of methodological complications (construct validity, lab-only outcomes, effect size, replication), the author's own study, then policy implications

articles.title: Sweeteners and the quest for the perfect alternative to sugar
articles.note: researcher-written: opens on the authors' own trial-design problem (a biscuit), long history of sweeteners, a policy section, an evidence-literacy section on why studies disagree, then a trial-by-trial walk through randomised evidence; the closing line returns to the opening biscuit

articles.title: The truth about child IQ: research shows it fluctuates and may be an unreliable predictor of future success
articles.note: researcher-written evidence tour framed by Mozart (myth-busting open, Mozart close); seven crossheaded sections each pairing a meta-analysis or cohort with its implication; a personal childhood scene midway introduces the nature-nurture complication

articles.title: Our quest to find a truly Earth-like planet in deep space
articles.note: researcher-written: discovery scene of the first exoplanet, a long history-of-ideas section, a techniques explainer, then the authors' own observing campaigns told as first-person scenes leading to measured masses; closes on the Earth-twin quest with a one-line kicker

articles.title: I investigated millions of tweets from the Kremlin’s ‘troll factory’ and discovered classic propaganda techniques reimagined for the social media age
articles.note: researcher-written: long institutional backstory (founder, whistleblowers) before the author's own corpus study; then one crossheaded section per case study (election, Covid, Crimea) built from analysis results and example posts; ends on platform policy and AI-era outlook

articles.title: Static electricity is a mystery, and scientists are all charged up
articles.note: lab-bench scene, nut graf on an unsolved basic phenomenon, explainer and history sections, then one experimental thread (bead levitation, surface contamination) with method then findings; a conference serves as recurring scene and the close returns to it

articles.title: Why Epstein-Barr is the ‘everything virus’
articles.note: six-paragraph patient scene before the nut graf; discovery history, then the key cohort study (military blood samples) told as a 20-year puzzle with method before result; mechanism section on two hypotheses; treatment and vaccine pipeline; closes back on the patient

articles.title: Will the U.S. megadrought ever end?
articles.note: opens on one town running out of water, nut graf on the regional drought and a contested new study; tree-ring and model studies follow, each method then finding, plus a mechanism block on the Pacific oscillation; returns to the town and its grocer at the end

articles.title: Have we entered a new age of AI-enabled scientific discovery?
articles.note: trend feature organised by a recurring metaphor (AI searching inside a box); each section pairs a researcher case with a skeptic's caveat; studies appear as short case results (a small drug trial, a planet-orbit experiment), not as extended method-finding runs

articles.title: Species Slowdown: Is Nature’s Ability to Self-Repair Stalling?
articles.note: news-analysis structure: the result in the first sentence, one method paragraph, outside reactions and a dissenting dataset, then a long history-of-ideas detour (stability versus churn) that explains why the result matters, ending on what it means for conservation

articles.title: The Upper Atmosphere Is Cooling, Prompting New Climate Concerns
articles.note: paradox lede and nut graf (good news, new worries), a mechanism explainer, then a tour of consequences (satellites, ozone, weather), each built from one measurement or study; closes on the threat to data supply with a callback to the opening coinage

articles.title: All the Fish We Cannot See
articles.note: historical sonar mystery as the opening scene, three-paragraph nut graf ending on a question, then researcher-by-researcher threads (counting fish, respiration, poop sinking rates), each a method-complication-finding loop; turns to fisheries history and policy, closing on humility

articles.title: Conjuring the Lost Land Beneath the North Sea
articles.note: place-led opening (an industrialised sea) and a nut graf that reframes a 'land bridge' as a homeland; long century-spanning history, then one researcher's seismic-mapping and sediment-DNA programme told method-first with a single artefact as the payoff object; closes on climate migration then and now

articles.title: Chemical Conversations Between Forests and the Sky Affect Air Quality, Clouds, and More
articles.note: researcher-written review: question lede, then eight short crossheaded sections moving from mechanism to climate paradox, health, urban policy, modelling problems and new satellite tools; findings come as one-sentence citations of meta-analyses and models; no scenes, no quoted voices

articles.title: How Gratitude Changes You and Your Brain
articles.note: researcher-written report of one randomised trial: question, method, headline result inside the first six paragraphs, then four numbered crossheads, each a secondary finding followed by a 'what this means for you' paragraph; no scenes or outside voices

articles.title: Do Africa’s Mass Animal Migrations Extend Into Deep Time?
articles.note: researcher-written first-person: herd scene, the field's assumption, and the overturning answer up front; background, then the author's isotope method told as a lab scene, an expected-versus-found finding, corroborating studies, and conservation implications; closing image returns to the herd

articles.title: Can In-Utero Exposure to Acetaminophen Cause Autism and ADHD?
articles.note: evidence-weighing feature hung on a lawsuit: consensus statement versus rebuttals up front, drug history and alternatives, then the observational evidence followed by a long run of methodological complications (recall, heredity, confounding by indication) and one reanalysis that erases the effect; ends on what everyone agrees on and the studies still needed

articles.title: Road Hazard: Evidence Mounts on Toxic Pollution from Tires
articles.note: opens on a solved mystery (salmon die-offs traced to one tyre chemical) and widens to tyre pollution generally; the middle stacks measurements of scale and exposure, each often a single figure from a study or company test; ends on regulation and engineering fixes

articles.title: Antimicrobial Resistance Is Killing Millions. Climate Change Is Making It Worse.
articles.note: two patient stories run through the piece as recurring scenes; between them, short mechanism explainers each carried by an expert quote; studies appear as single-sentence citations; heavy on voice, thin on method; ends on global policy
